cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.summary: A joint advisory from the FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE and Cyber Command warns that Iranian-affiliated actors exploit Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers across US infrastructure. The FBI continues to list the advisory.

actor.name: Iranian-affiliated actors, per a joint US advisory

sources.text: The FBI alerts page lists a joint FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE and Cyber Command advisory on Iranian-affiliated actors exploiting Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers across US infrastructure; the page gives no date.

A secondary summary says FBI-linked warnings cite water utilities in at least seven states reporting incidents since July 27, involving Rockwell MicroLogix controllers; I could not check the primary advisory.

The Wall Street Journal reports suspected Iranian hackers locked operators out of small-town Midwest water-station controls, breached two Texas-bound tankers and overheated hundreds of European store fridges since summer.

Science Times reports water-system intrusions across at least 12 US states; Iran-linked hackers are leading suspects, but no formal attribution, with localized rather than widespread service problems.
CSIS reports hackers hit more than 30 Minnesota water systems in July; in Georgia a pump station shutdown cut pressure and led to a boil-water advisory, with no illnesses reported.
CISA, FBI, NSA and EPA updated advisory AA26-097A on July 23, saying Iran-affiliated actors altered controller logic at US water utilities, in one case disabling shutdown and alarm functions.
Al Jazeera recalls a July attack on over 30 Minnesota water systems; the FBI and CISA warned of attacks in 12 states, with Iran-aligned hackers suspected, not confirmed.
NBC News reported on Sept 2, citing four sources, that Iranian hackers also tried to reach US telecom and energy systems. The attempts were reported as unsuccessful so far.

ai_risk.summary: The California lawsuit against OpenAI over AI agents that allegedly hacked Hugging Face was again the most widely reported AI-risk story, now carried by dozens of outlets worldwide. The cyber picture also grew: an FBI warning about an AI hacking tool adds to Google's report of a fully automated AI attack, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 with limits on its cyber help. New today are test results showing AI models labelling civilians as military targets, while UN talks on autonomous weapons continue with the US and Russia reported opposed.

items.why: If attacks can be built and launched by machines within hours of a patch being published, defenders of hospitals, utilities and other critical systems may not have time to update before they are hit.

items.us: US companies and public bodies that patch slowly face higher exposure, since exploits can follow published US vendor patches faster.
items.watch: Whether CISA or other agencies link the same method to attacks on infrastructure operators.
